meta.title: Babylon c. 575 BCE (reign of Nebuchadnezzar II), true-scale layout for the v2 three.js world
meta.date: -0575 (c. 575 BCE as the conventional label): the completed city LATE IN THE REIGN of Nebuchadnezzar II (604-562), incl. the final glazed Ishtar Gate (Level 1)
meta.dateNote: Pedersen dates the Level-1 gate, the North Gate, the limestone north wall and the Summer Palace to the end of the reign; an archaeomagnetic study (Di Chiara et al., PLoS ONE 2024, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0293014) gives 569 BCE as the best-fit firing date of the gate bricks. A strict 575 could still be the Level-2 gate (flat glaze, no lions). The towered river wall that Pedersen pairs with this phase is deliberately left out as later.
meta.season: late April / early May (barley harvest), solar declination +15 deg. The river is modelled at its mean level (-3.0), not at the spring flood stage (about -1.5).
meta.units: metres; 1 unit = 1 m; true scale, no compression
meta.axes: +x = grid east, +z = grid south, +y = up; axes follow the CITY GRID (Processional Way beside the precinct / inner walls)
meta.gridRotationDirection: grid north (-z) points 15.8 deg WEST of true north (true azimuth 344.2)
meta.azimuthConvention: model azimuth: 0 = -z (grid north), 90 = +x (grid east), clockwise. modelAzimuth = trueAzimuth + 15.8
meta.rotationConvention: footprint.rotationDeg is clockwise seen from above; three.js rotation.y = -rotationDeg*PI/180. True-cardinal buildings have rotationDeg = +15.5
meta.polygonConvention: all "polygon" rings are explicitly closed (first vertex repeated); coordinates are [x, z]
meta.verticalDatum: y = level in the German excavation datum (0 = 25.5 m a.s.l.). Water plane y = -3.0

worldExtent.note: ground and sky to the horizon; no visible edge

meta.src: R1 1, 12; R2 12.1; R3 2; harmonised to R1 convention

bridgeReach.form: CONJECTURAL: Nebuchadnezzar's quay is not attested next to the bridge (never built there, or pulled down later). Within about 25 m either side of the bridge axis show the older Nabopolassar quay as the river front: c. 3.9 m thick, top +2.0, rounded corners, the street running flush onto the bridge; the +4.0 upper wall of the Nebuchadnezzar quay ends in a return on either side.

river.excluded: the towered "Nabonidus" river wall and bridge-head gate (after c. 560 BCE) are NOT modelled; R1's east-bank line beside the precinct followed that later wall and is replaced by R3's quay

crossingAtPW.form: CONJECTURAL: the street runs c. 14 m above the canal water on a made causeway; the canal passes under it through a baked-brick culvert / arched opening c. 3 m wide and c. 22 m long with brick retaining walls on both sides (NOT a free-standing viaduct)
crossingAtPW.basis: the bridge (titurru) is textual only; 150-180 m of the street were washed away by a later river channel (R2 7.1, 7.3; Pedersen 2021 p. 218)

canals.note: Excavated from the river to the middle of the palace south wall. East of the Processional Way the course is conjectural (washed away by a later flood); drawn ESE to the east moat through a culvert under the walls.

east.lineNote: innerLine = centreline of Imgur-Enlil. Rev. 1 moved it 7-8.5 m south on the north side and 2-12 m west on the east side (profiles on Pedersen Figs. 6.2 and 2.2); the south wall was unchanged. Nemetti-Enlil and the quay keep the excavated section (12.3 and 31-36.75 m outward); Pedersen's plans draw the two walls c. 16 m apart centre to centre near the gate, 3-4 m more than that section.

raisedSection.why: Nebuchadnezzar raised the palace quarter and the gate by 12-15 m; the city walls there were raised with the terrain (Pedersen 2021 pp. 30, 59; preserved tops +13.5 / +14.5). Swept at the standard levels the wall-walk (+14) would lie BELOW the gate pavement (+15.4).

raisedSection.stepDown: between x = 450 and x = 650 both walls step down at each tower (seven bays of 27.6 m, about 2.2 m per bay). Interpolate linearly between the stations for a tower's walk level. Length and form of the step-down are DESIGN VALUES: unattested.
raisedSection.visibleFoot: the walls are founded at about 0 but stand in made ground here: the visible foot is the local terrain (South Palace floor +12.5 and North Palace terrace +8 / +15 west of the gate; +15.4 at the gate; Ninmah temple floor +12; falling to about +3 at x = 700)

outside.falls: both fall with the walls to the standard +1.5 / +4.0 at x = 650
outside.note: east of the gate the embankment (quay line) forms the south side of the East Fortification; Pedersen assumes its top at +15 here, 5 m above the walkway behind it

landUseRule.rule: field zones are the COMPLEMENT of everything else: a point belongs to the first class in this list that contains it
priority: wall zones (inner: 12 m inside to the quay line; outer: 4 m inside to 27 m outside the mud-wall centreline)

landUseRule.gardenVegetablesNote: small green plots (onion, garlic, cress, flax) only directly at canals and ditches; sesame is a SUMMER crop: at the barley harvest those plots are bare or freshly sown, never green

#4F7A34 garden vegetables / onion-garlic / flax (small plots at canals only)

rules: city walls, houses: mud plaster (8 tones above, +/-12 % value jitter, mixed within every block); NO colour on city walls
white lime wash on WALLS and parapet faces only: temples, precinct, Esagila, 45 % of elite houses, 15 % of ordinary houses
ALL roofs are rolled mud on palm beams: roofEarth #BBA987 (albedo 0.40-0.48), never white; whitewashed houses show white only on wall and parapet faces
bare baked brick (yellow-buff to light red, thin dark or white joints): palaces, quays, bridge piers, ziggurat, Ishtar Gate wings, street walls above the lion frieze

blue glaze ONLY on: Ishtar Gate, lion-frieze band and merlons of the street walls north of it (merlons textually certain for the North Palace only; assumed on the east street wall), ziggurat summit temple, South Palace throne-room court facade and inner gate towers, North Palace merlons
never use the museum green: it is decayed RED glaze
value targets (albedo): limewashed wall and parapet faces 0.62-0.72, mud roofs 0.40-0.48, mud walls 0.38-0.50, streets 0.28-0.35, court floors 0.30
colour accents about one per 3-4 houses: dyed cloth on roofs, awnings, painted door frames, garden green, goods
palette.conf: medium (suggested sRGB starting points, not measurements)

lighting.sunFormula: modelAzimuth = trueAzimuth + 15.8; dirToSun = (sin(az)*cos(el), sin(el), -cos(az)*cos(el)) with az = model azimuth

golden.lights: the sun stands in the grid WNW-NW: west faces fully lit; the river glitter path points towards a camera looking WNW. At 11 deg the walled lion street is a shadow canyon (pavement and both friezes shaded, the gate front lit only above 7-11 m): street and gate shots use the afternoon state instead
golden.conf: high (sun geometry); medium (colours, from the reference)

afternoon.lights: used for the lion street and the Ishtar Gate (shots 2-3): at 24.8 deg the east lion frieze is sunlit down to 1.7 m, the east half of the gate front down to 1.5-6.7 m (n.s on the gate front = 0.30); the west frieze stays in open shade with strong bounce from the lit east wall
afternoon.conf: high (sun geometry); medium (colours: golden state interpolated toward a warm afternoon)

morning.lights: sun from the grid east (slightly south): east faces lit, south faces raked (ziggurat stairs, saw-tooth house fronts), mist over river and canals

moon.note: rev. 1: az 140 / el 38 implied a lunar declination 7 deg further south than a waxing gibbous moon can have on this date

fires.where: INSIDE courtyards and on roofs (no street windows), door spill in lanes; fixed fires (braziers, torches) ONLY at city gates, wall towers, the precinct gates, the bridge heads, the palace gate and walls and in temple courts; fire bowls on the ziggurat terraces (conjectural, after a Seleucid night-vigil ritual from Uruk); open oil lamps or small braziers on moored boats (no lanterns: enclosed lamps are not attested). Streets, incl. the Processional Way, are dark.

blue.rule: no purple/magenta cast; darkness is the rule; streets are black, light leaks upward from courts
blue.conf: high (sun geometry); medium (palette); low (number of lamps)

lighting.transitions: mode changes animate the sun along its arc over 1.5-3 s (sky, fog, exposure, fire emissive and stars follow one parameter); never a cross-fade of two looks
lighting.shadows: cascaded shadow maps (4 x 4096), 0.3-0.5 m penumbra near, plus baked vertex AO in lanes and courts

shots.path: ONE continuous camera path: eased fly-through transitions (centripetal Catmull-Rom on position and target, ease-in-out), slow drift during holds; no cuts
shots.pathSpline: inside a shot the position moves on the STRAIGHT segment between its keyframes (eased). Each transition is a centripetal Catmull-Rom (alpha 0.5) through [last keyframe of the previous shot, transitionWaypoints..., first keyframe of the shot]; its outer tangent neighbours are the previous shot's second-to-last keyframe and the shot's second keyframe. tools/validate_world.py samples exactly these curves against the height model.
shots.keyframeFormat: t = seconds from the start of the shot; the transition flies from the previous shot's last pose through transitionWaypoints (positions only, evenly timed) to the first keyframe (t = transitionIn)
shots.clearanceRule: at least 2 m above monuments, walls and the bridge everywhere; below roof level inside the inner city only over water, on a street axis, over the precinct court or on the declared roof
